To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“The edge functionalization of a nanographite with a serinolin derivative containing a pyrole ring and the subsequent formation of the adduct between the obtained material and chitosan led to the ultra-high exfoliated graphene-based materials in water, stable for months in organic solvents, in water and in solvents with solubility parameters in the range from ca. 8 to 14 (MPa) 1/2.”

a nanosized graphene (HSAG) can be exfoliated in a water-based medium in the presence of a polymer such as CS, thanks to the synergy of the edge functionalization of the graphene layers with a serinolylic derivative and the presence of the polymer.
the synergy between an edge functionalized graphene layer and a chitosan (biopolymer) led to the ultra-high exfoliations in water and in organic solvents of a nanoscaled graphite (HSAG).
In summary, our research is concerned with

the exfoliation of graphite in water in the form of a stable dispersion in the presence of a chitosan (CH) derivative and with the preparation of aerogels and carbon papers from the obtained dispersion.
the preparation of a graphene-based nanocomposite with ultra-high exfoliaton in water, in the presence of chitosan.
the development of new graphene materials, with a particular attention to their exfoliation in aqueous media and the preparation of new graphene-based composites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a simple and straightforward preparation method of a nanographite–polymer adduct in water was obtained by exploiting the synergistic action between a nanographite functionalized with hydroxyl groups at its edge and a biobased polymer such as CS.

the edge functionalization of a nanographite, HSAG, with a serinole derivative, SP, and the formation of a simple adduct between the functionalized nanographites and a biobased polymer, CS, are the key points for obtaining a stable water dispersion of graphene-based nanomaterials, which are the starting point for the preparation of carbon papers and aerogel composites.
the HSAG–SP adduct is a very promising nanosized graphite for exfoliation in the presence of chitosan.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a nanosized graphene material was exfoliated in a sustainable manner and in water, a very difficult task.
a moderately functional graphene layer can be easily exfoliated in the presence of chitosan.
the synergy between the edge functionalized graphene layers (SP) and CS led to a simple and sustainable preparation route of carbon papers and aerogel composites.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the exfoliation of nanographite is strongly enhanced in water in the case of a nanographite functionalized with hydroxyl groups at the edges and in the case of the presence of a biobased polymer such as CS.

the exfoliation of graphite in water in the form of stable dispersions can be obtained with a nanosized material, which is the most important feature for the preparation of graphene-based composites with a low environmental impact.
the edge functionalization of graphite layers with serinol pyrole (SP) and the addition of CS are a powerful tool to obtain ultra-high exfoliations in water.
